description: We are a team made up of a mathematics teacher and students who are enthusiastic about programming, science, and technology. We share curiosity, creativity, and a strong desire to learn through new challenges. We want to participate in this hackathon to experience something different, put our skills to the test, work collaboratively, and discover how we can use our knowledge to develop innovative solutions to real-world problems.
summary:
ZeroFlame makes NASA’s microgravity combustion research easier to explore. Users can visualize, group, and compare 24 studies across three areas of fire safety: prevention, detection, and extinguishment. The platform distinguishes connections documented in the sources from those inferred by the team.

Also, you can find Fire Protocol: 0G, ZeroFlame’s first educational game, players control a robot, adjust airflow to extinguish a flame, and investigate how it ignited. A debrief links each mission to NASA’s BASS-II experiments. Other studies in the catalog could inspire future games about fire safety in space.
details:
ZeroFlame is an interactive web platform designed to visualize, compare, and group NASA's microgravity combustion research, making complex scientific information more accessible and easier to compare. This page organizes data from 24 scientific investigations, allowing users to explore experimental objectives, analyze testing conditions, and identify similarities through mathematical algorithms. It also connects research findings to three key areas of fire safety: prevention, detection, and extinguishment, distinguishing between evidence-based and inferred connections to ensure scientific transparency.

The platform also includes Fire Protocol: 0G, a pixel-art game inspired by NASA’s BASS-II experiments. Players control a robot, adjust airflow to put out a flame, and inspect evidence to identify how the sample ignited. After each mission, a scientific debrief connects the gameplay to the documented experiment and explains which elements were adapted for the game.

By pairing an interactive research catalog with a playable scenario, ZeroFlame gives students and other curious users two ways to explore how fire behaves in microgravity and why these findings matter for spacecraft safety.
